Context/Background:
We leverage a clinical trial that compared neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 (Nivo), anti-PD-1+CTLA-4 (Nivo+Ipi), and anti-PD-1+LAG-3 (Nivo+Rela) therapies in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma patients. Combination therapies promote higher pathologic response rates versus monotherapy, and major pathologic response is associated with better survival. To address whether successful immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) regimens act through similar or distinct pathways, we robustly and longitudinally characterize transcriptional and proteomic dynamics of CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) in a clonal manner. 

Thirty-eight patients were evaluable for pathologic tumor response (pTR) and categorized into three groups following previous studies: pTR-0 (91–100% viable residual tumor), pTR-1 (51%–90% viable residual tumor), and pTR-2 (≤50% viable residual tumor. 

To study the association between transcriptional dynamics of T cells and pathologic responses to neoadjuvant ICI treatments, we isolated and profiled 372,914 CD45+CD3+ TIL from 35 patients (29 baseline and 31 post-surgical fresh tumor specimens; 20 patients having matched pre- and post-treatment biopsies), using the 10x Genomics 5′ scRNA-seq workflow. These cells were clustered into five distinct populations annotated as CD8+ T, CD4+ T, FOXP3+ T, γδ T/MAIT and cycling T cell clusters, and visualized by Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) analysis. Clusters were annotated based on the expression of reported canonical T cell marker gene and CITE-seq expression levels.
Prompt:
We analyzed the clusters of CD3+ TIL and found that the proportion of baseline CD8+ TIL showed a trend to the more frequent in responding patients.  When we assessed baseline expression of PDCD1, CTLA4, and LAG3 by CD8+ TIL, we observed the highest expression for PDCD1 and LAG3. The expression of PDCD1 and LAG3 by baseline CD8+ TIL positively correlated with the degree of pathologic response only in Nivo+Rela-treated patients. Similar analyses did not show a significant correlation between LAG3, PDCD1 and CTLA4 expression levels in baseline CD8+ TIL and the degree of pathologic response in the Nivo and Nivo+Ipi cohorts.

To identify baseline CD8+ TIL transcriptional signatures correlating with pathologic response, we generated a list of differentially expressed genes (DEG) between pTR-2 and pTR-0 tumors for each regimen.

Based on the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between pTR-2 and pTR-0 tumors for the Nivo+Ipi and Nivo+Rela cohorts, generate a summary describing the key transcriptional signatures, functional categories, and immune pathways enriched in pTR-2 vs pTR-0 tumors. Highlight representative genes and link them to their biological roles.  Focus on T cell–specific functional programs and gene modules defined by known immune states.

Introduction/Context  
Neoadjuvant CD8⁺ TIL from head and neck squamous-cell carcinoma (HNSCC) patients treated with anti-PD-1 alone (Nivo), anti-PD-1+CTLA-4 (Nivo+Ipi), or anti-PD-1+LAG-3 (Nivo+Rela) were profiled by 5′ scRNA-seq at baseline. Patients were stratified by pathologic response (pTR-0: 91–100% viable tumor; pTR-1: 51–90%; pTR-2: ≤50%). Here, we compare baseline CD8⁺ TIL transcriptional signatures between pTR-2 and pTR-0 for the Nivo+Ipi and Nivo+Rela arms.  

Keywords  
•  Interferon Response  
•  Ribosome/Translation  
•  T-cell Receptor Signaling  
•  Th17/Th1 Differentiation  
•  Immune Checkpoints  

Candidate Genes  
PDCD1, LAG3, MX1, CXCL13, ISG15  

1) Pathway Enrichments: Nivo+Rela (pTR-2 vs pTR-0)  
• ORA (KEGG_2021_Human) up in pTR-2:  
  – Th17 cell differentiation  
  – Th1 and Th2 cell differentiation  
  – T cell receptor signaling pathway  
  – PD-L1/PD-1 checkpoint in cancer  
  – Antigen processing & presentation  
• GSEA (MSigDB_Hallmark_2020) strong up:  
  – Interferon-γ Response (NES 5.76)  
  – Interferon-α Response (NES 4.07)  
  – Complement (moderate)  
• GSEA strong down:  
  – Translation and ribosome biogenesis (GO)  
  – Metabolism of proteins (Reactome)  

Counts by database (Nivo+Rela GSEA)  
KEGG_2016: 62% up (5/8) | GO_BP_2023: 74% up (35/47) | Reactome_2024: 16% up (10/63) | Hallmark_2020: 57% up (4/7)  

Table 1. Top enriched themes (Nivo+Rela)  
KEGG_2021_Human (UP)  
| Theme                                 | Leading Genes                              |  
|---------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|  
| Th17 cell differentiation             | STAT3, NFATC3, RORyT, HIF1A, IL21R           |  
| T cell receptor signaling             | CD3E, ZAP70, LCK, CTLA4, PDCD1               |  
| PD-1 checkpoint pathway in cancer     | PDCD1, CTLA4, CD274, JAK2, STAT1             |  

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (UP)  
| Theme                       | Leading Genes                              |  
|-----------------------------|---------------------------------------------|  
| Interferon-γ Response       | MX1, STAT1, ISG15, IRF7, OAS1               |  
| Interferon-α Response       | MX1, IFI6, IFI44L, BST2, ADAR               |  

Reactome_Pathways_2024 (DOWN)  
| Theme                        | Leading Genes                             |  
|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|  
| Metabolism of Proteins       | RPL5, RPS23, RPS18, RPL30, RPL32           |  
| Translation                   | RPS18, RPL36, RPS28, RPS21, RPL5           |  

2) Pathway Enrichments: Nivo+Ipi (pTR-2 vs pTR-0)  
• ORA (KEGG_2021_Human) up in pTR-2:  
  – Ribosome  
  – Coronavirus disease (ribosomal component)  
  – T cell receptor signaling (weaker)  
• GSEA (KEGG_2016) strong up:  
  – Ribosome (NES 6.33)  
  – Oxidative phosphorylation, Parkinson’s disease (mitochondrial)  
• GSEA down:  
  – Transcriptional misregulation in cancer  

Counts by database (Nivo+Ipi GSEA)  
KEGG_2016: 34% up (12/35) | GO_BP_2023: 32% up (42/132) | Reactome_2024: 67% up (108/161) | Hallmark_2020: 50% up (5/10)  

Table 2. Top enriched themes (Nivo+Ipi)  
KEGG_2016 (UP)  
| Theme                        | Leading Genes                        |  
|------------------------------|---------------------------------------|  
| Ribosome                     | RPS26, RPS23, RPL30, RPL36A, RPS5     |  
| Oxidative phosphorylation    | NDUFB11, COX7A2, COX6A1, UQCRB, ATP6V |  

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (DOWN)  
| Theme                        | Leading Genes                        |  
|------------------------------|---------------------------------------|  
| UV Response Dn               | FYN, DUSP1, PTEN, RUNX1               |  

3) Targeted (keyword-guided) subset  
Nivo+Rela ORA filtered on “Interferon” and “T cell receptor”:  
| Gene_set              | Term                                  | Adjusted P-value |  
|-----------------------|---------------------------------------|------------------|  
| MSigDB_Hallmark_2020  | Interferon Gamma Response             | 3.4 × 10⁻⁷       |  
| KEGG_2021_Human       | T cell receptor signaling pathway     | 4.5 × 10⁻¹²      |  

Nivo+Ipi ORA filtered on “Ribosome”:  
| Gene_set           | Term       | Adjusted P-value |  
|--------------------|------------|------------------|  
| KEGG_2021_Human    | Ribosome   | 7.17 × 10⁻⁵⁵     |  

4) Key Genes/Proteins (leading-edge)  
Up in pTR-2 (Nivo+Rela)  
| Gene    | Role/Function                       | Pathway(s)                      |  
|---------|-------------------------------------|---------------------------------|  
| MX1     | Antiviral effector (IFN-stimulated) | IFN-α/IFN-γ Responses           |  
| STAT1   | Interferon-activated TF             | IFN-γ Response, TCR signaling   |  
| ISG15   | Ubiquitin-like modifier             | Interferon Response             |  
| LAG3    | Exhaustion checkpoint receptor      | TCR signaling, Immune checkpt.  |  
| CXCL13  | B-cell chemoattractant              | Tfh/Th1 differentiation         |  

Down in pTR-2 (Nivo+Rela)  
| Gene    | Role/Function                       | Pathway(s)                      |  
|---------|-------------------------------------|---------------------------------|  
| RPS18   | 40S ribosomal subunit               | Translation, Ribosome           |  
| RPL5    | 60S ribosomal subunit               | Translation, Ribosome           |  
| EEF1B2  | Elongation factor                   | Translation                     |  

5) Comparisons  
• Nivo+Rela pTR-2: dominated by interferon signaling, Th differentiation, antigen presentation, and checkpoint-receptor up-regulation—hallmarks of an activated/exhausted CD8⁺ TIL state. Translation machinery is selectively down-modulated, consistent with a shift from proliferation to effector programs.  
• Nivo+Ipi pTR-2: marked by elevated ribosomal and mitochondrial gene expression, suggesting heightened protein synthesis and metabolic output but weaker Interferon/TCR signatures.  

6) Implications & Next Steps  
• The strong IFN-γ/α and TCR-signaling enrichment in Nivo+Rela responders implicates robust T-cell activation and exhaustion markers (LAG3, PDCD1). In contrast, Nivo+Ipi responders skew toward biosynthetic/metabolic remodeling.  
• Follow-up:  
  1. Validate IFN-signature at protein/CITE-seq level in Nivo+Rela CD8⁺ TIL (e.g., STAT1 phosphorylation).  
  2. Assess functional cytotoxicity and clonality of CXCL13⁺ and LAG3⁺ CD8⁺ subsets.  
  3. Test whether translation suppression (ribosomal down-regulation) in Nivo+Rela links to memory formation versus terminal exhaustion.  
  4. Examine whether metabolic (OxPhos) programs in Nivo+Ipi relate to distinct differentiation states (e.g., TCF1⁺ progenitor cells).
